title: Better words, a weaker point
chapter: Can’t See the Forest for the Trees
lines: An AI improved the author’s sentences, and quietly weakened what he was trying to say.
That experience opens Can't See the Forest for the Trees, a book about systems that miss the damage they cause.

emotionalPlan.purpose: Keep the manuscript before and after editing, preserving a visibly missing emphatic passage rather than inventing a quote.
voiceDirections: Speak with personal disappointment; give gentle emphasis to weakened what he was trying to say. Keep a natural conversational voice, let the listener picture this specific situation, and leave a real pause at the end.
Speak with clear interest; give gentle emphasis to damage they cause. Keep a natural conversational voice, let the listener picture this specific situation, and leave a real pause at the end.

title: When smoothing conceals tension
chapter: An edit can lose the argument
lines: The sentences sounded reasonable while doubt, urgency, and responsibility became easier to overlook.
The book follows a similar pattern in companies, research, politics, and the technologies connecting them.

emotionalPlan.purpose: Use one smoothing transition and stop; let the lost edge remain perceptible.
voiceDirections: Speak with quiet unease; give gentle emphasis to responsibility. Keep a natural conversational voice, let the listener picture this specific situation, and leave a real pause at the end.
Speak with engaged clarity; give gentle emphasis to similar pattern. Keep a natural conversational voice, let the listener picture this specific situation, and leave a real pause at the end.

title: Who sees the whole?
lines: Each specialist can tend a necessary part while the consequences of the whole escape attention.

title: Return to the missing edge
lines: A smoother explanation can make a real conflict harder to notice, and harder to name.
